newsitem.title: USA: Extra Canadian lumber not seen affecting US prices.
newsitem.headline: Extra Canadian lumber not seen affecting US prices.

text.p: Lumber industry sources doubt that an additional 50 million to 100 million board feet of lumber that may enter the U.S. from Canada this year would affect lumber prices.
"I don't think any consequential amounts are involved," said Mike Flannery, president of Pope and Talbot Inc, a Portland, Oregon-based lumber manufacturer.
Flannery said the extra amount of lumber is small compared to the 14.7 billion board feet allowed in annually under a five-year U.S.-Canadian lumber agreement.

On Tuesday, Ronald McDonald, parliamentary secretary to International Trade Minister Art Eggleton, said in Ottawa that small Canadian lumber companies could ship lumber to the U.S. in excess of their quota and apply it to quotas for future years.
"We anticipate that there will could be between 50 and 100 million board feet requested on the draw forward provision," McDonald said.
"That's not a lot," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney lumber analyst, who expects lumber prices to trend higher.
"I think the January has some more upside potential," he said, referring to the CME January lumber futures contract.
The CME January contract rose the maximum $15.00 per thousand board feet daily limit Tuesday to $419.40, and Schmaedick said further gains are likely.
"I think January will trade in a range from $380 to $440, probably for the next couple of weeks," he said.
